source: NCERT Class VIII, Social and Political Life III, Polity Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. Why Parliament
points: **Parliament** enables citizens to take part in decision-making and to **control the government** — the heart of a democracy.
The idea of **people's approval** grew during the freedom struggle (people wanted a say in how they were governed).
Every adult has the **right to vote** — **universal adult franchise** — to elect representatives.

sections.heading: 2. Structure of Parliament
points: Parliament of India has **two Houses**:

sub: **Lok Sabha (House of the People)** — members (**MPs**) **directly elected** by the people from constituencies; term **5 years**.
**Rajya Sabha (Council of States)** — represents the **States**; members mostly elected by State legislatures; a **permanent** House (⅓ retire every 2 years).

points: The **President of India** is also a part of Parliament.
The party/coalition with a **majority in the Lok Sabha** forms the government; its leader = **Prime Minister**.

sections.heading: 3. Roles of Parliament
points: **To select the national government** — the majority party forms the executive; the rest form the **Opposition**.
**To control, guide and inform the government** — through the **Question Hour**, debates and discussions; ministers are **accountable** to Parliament.
**Law-making** — Parliament is the highest **law-making** body.

sections.heading: 4. How a Law is Made
points: A proposed law = a **Bill**; it is **debated and voted** in **both Houses**.
After both Houses pass it, it goes to the **President** for **assent**, then becomes an **Act (law)**.
Citizens, the media and pressure groups can influence law-making (e.g. the **Domestic Violence Act, 2005**).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Parliament = Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha + President.
Lok Sabha = directly elected (5-yr term); Rajya Sabha = represents states, permanent House.
Majority party in Lok Sabha forms government; leader = PM; rest = Opposition.
Roles: select government, control/inform it (Question Hour), make laws.
Bill → passed by both Houses → President's assent → Act.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Lok Sabha** members are **directly elected**; **Rajya Sabha** members represent the **states** (mostly indirectly elected).
The **Rajya Sabha is a permanent House** (not dissolved; ⅓ retire every 2 years).
A Bill needs to pass **both Houses** and get **Presidential assent** to become an Act.
The **PM** leads the majority party in the **Lok Sabha**.
